### Scope verdict

`project-in-scope ✅` — CV-CUDA is a CUDA-consuming C/C++/Python project, not a CUDA reimplementation and not a compiler/driver project. Structural scan found 1,528 C/C++/Python source/header files, 214 CUDA `.cu`/`.cuh` files including submodules/tests, and no disqualifying alternate-language manifest.

### Graph notes

- Core source-port scope: `src/cvcuda/priv` (70 `.cu`, 8 `.cuh`) plus required local cuda_tools/legacy host-driver closure.
- Vendored/benchmark CUDA: `3rdparty/nvbench` has 55 `.cu` and 66 `.cuh`; treat as benchmark-only and disable unless explicit benchmark migration is requested.
- PTX rule: structural scan found no project inline PTX / `.ptx` / `asm volatile` hits in source scope. The MTX rewrite how-to was still read because PTX/ptxas is in the ecosystem graph; if later build failures mention PTX, follow `auto-musify-skills/musa-mtx-rewrite/SKILL.md` five-step semantic reconstruction workflow.

### Capability Support Matrix

No generic runtime codec/hwaccel/plugin registry is exposed as a required MUSA capability surface in the core C++ library. CV-CUDA itself is row 38 in the counterpart matrix with **no drop-in MUSA equivalent**, so the project is a source migration, not an SDK swap. Operator API registration is project-local; entries should only be exposed when their real MUSA implementation is compiled. Unsupported or unported operators must be disabled with explicit `musify: disabled` markers or allowed to fail with root cause; do not mechanically preserve CUDA-era tables.

| surface_id | surface_kind | declaration_paths | registry_paths | allowed_entries | disabled_entries | unknown_entries | registration_policy | validation_signal | source_note |
|------------|--------------|-------------------|----------------|-----------------|------------------|-----------------|---------------------|------------------|-------------|
| cvcuda_operator_api | api-dispatch-table | `src/cvcuda/include/cvcuda/Op*.h`, `src/cvcuda/Op*.cpp` | `src/cvcuda/CMakeLists.txt`, `src/cvcuda/priv/CMakeLists.txt` | Operators with compiled real MUSA source-port | Operators blocked by unmapped API (e.g. `OpFindHomography` if muSOLVER mismatch persists) | Any operator not built/tested on MUSA | register only real compiled implementation; no stubs | gtest `cvcuda_test_system*`, Python op tests if `BUILD_PYTHON=ON` | counterpart row 38: CV-CUDA has no SDK equivalent; source-port required |
| optional_python_interop | plugin/interop-sample | `samples/interoperability/*.py`, `bench/python/*` | sample scripts, requirements files | PyTorch via torch_musa if enabled | CUDA Python/PyCUDA/CuPy paths unless replacement exists | nvImageCodec/PyNvVideoCodec samples unless runtime-selectable MUSA counterpart is actually wired | keep out of required total unless MUSA path exposed | sample script run / import checks | rows 35–36 partial media counterparts; rows 83–84 gaps |

## 3. Source and Build-System Findings

### Manifest scan

- Root CMake enables CUDA language and includes `ConfigCUDA`.
- Build options: `BUILD_TESTS`, `BUILD_TESTS_CPP`, `BUILD_TESTS_PYTHON`, `BUILD_TESTS_WHEELS`, `BUILD_BENCH`.
- `.gitmodules`: pybind11, googletest, dlpack (CUDA-free), nvbench (CUDA benchmark dependency).
- CMake links `CUDA::cusolver_static`, `CUDA::cublas_static`, `CUDA::cublasLt_static`; CUDA runtime and driver are pervasive through headers.

### Include/API scan

- 138 `.cu` and 76 `.cuh` across repository including tests/submodules.
- `cuda_runtime` signal in ~180 files; `cuda.h` signal in ~20 files.
- `curand` signal in 7 files; `cub/` in 10 files; `thrust/` in 8 files.
- No source-level `asm volatile`, `.ptx`, `ptxas`, `__shfl_sync`, or `__ballot_sync` hit in the structural scan output. Re-scan generated MUSA sources later.

### Vendored scan

- `3rdparty/nvbench` is the only CUDA-heavy vendored submodule; it should not block core migration.
- `pybind11`, `googletest`, `dlpack` are CUDA-free for migration purposes.

## 5. Python Conversion Strategy

`python_conversion_strategy: direct`

Rationale: CV-CUDA is a stable native C++/CUDA library with Python bindings; core port is CMake/source based. Python `torch.cuda.*` calls are limited to tests/samples (36 calls across 11 files), not central framework dispatch. No formal out-of-tree backend/plugin system or multi-vendor abstraction was detected.

| Factor | Value |
|--------|-------|
| 1. Upstream activity | 0 commits in last 90 days on local branch; current HEAD tag `v0.16.0` |
| 2. Vendor support | NVIDIA/CUDA-only in core; no `is_moore`, `torch_musa`, `torch_npu`, `torch_mlu` infra detected |
| 3. Fork maintenance cost | Medium; large C++ source port but no Python framework fork abstraction needed |
| 4. `torch.cuda.*` call count | 36 calls across 11 Python files, mainly samples/tests |
| 5. Existing vendor infra | none detected |
| 6. torchada upstream-ready | not applicable |

### Concerns / handoff notes

- Use parallel-folder porting: create MUSA siblings for CUDA source directories; leave `.cu`/`.cuh` originals unchanged.
- `OpFindHomography`/muSOLVER must be checked symbol-by-symbol; do not assume `cusolverDnSsyevjBatched` is drop-in.
- Warp-size assumptions and hardcoded masks may surface as correctness issues on S4000; verifier should prioritize affected operators (`Label`, `Histogram`, `Morphology`, `NMS`, `PairwiseMatcher`) if full tests are run.
- No Jira tickets and no publish push per user constraints.
